name: Active buzzer module (3-pin)
blurb: A buzzer board with its own oscillator: apply power to the signal pin and it beeps at a fixed pitch, no tone generation needed.

pins.name: VCC
pins.note: 3.3 to 5 V. The beep is louder at 5 V.

pins.name: I/O
pins.note: Most modules are low-level trigger: the buzzer sounds while this pin is LOW, so it beeps on power-up until the firmware sets the pin HIGH. Check yours.

verify: Highly variable layout. With calipers measure: board length and width, buzzer diameter and height (12 x 9.5 mm assumed), header position and pin order as printed, and mounting hole presence (none assumed). Confirm trigger polarity (low-level or high-level) with a multimeter. Sound hole size is a design value for the enclosure, not a measured one. PROJECT COPY: the library header box was removed from shapes because it covers the pad row in the booklet at every quarter turn (guide drawing check). Pads and outline are unchanged from the library file.
sources: No datasheet opened. Commonly reported size of 3-pin low-level-trigger buzzer modules (about 32 x 13 mm, 12 mm buzzer).
